topPRs.title: docs/ai: Add a deposit spec-conformance reviewer
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
Adds the third per-area specification-driven reviewer, after the derivation batch
reviewer and the interop reviewer. It follows the same thin-wrapper pattern: the
agent file holds the triggers, `docs/ai/spec-driven-review.md` holds the method,
and the new area guide holds scope, navigation, and domain checks. No protocol
rule is restated in the monorepo.

The area covers deposit derivation, the `0x7E` wire format, the L1 attributes and
upgrade deposits, execution rules that differ from a type-2 transaction, receipts,
and `OptimismPortal`.

Deposits are the next area by bug history and by loss severity. They hold the only
path that creates L2 ETH with no L2 source, so a wrong `mint` produces unbacked
supply. The two largest Immunefi payouts in the March to September 2026 window
shared one trigger: a permissionless over-cap deposit after Karst. Both were live
on OP Mainnet with the respected fault-proof prestate.

The specification defines deposit execution by difference from an EIP-1559
transaction. The guide therefore adds an explicit method for inherited rules: name
the upstream rule set, enumerate the OP exceptions, and check whether the
implementation still relies on an L1 invariant that an exception removes. That
class of defect produces no local diff.

topPRs.title: ci: run each crate's doc tests in isolation under cargo hack
topPRs.author: einar-oplabs
topPRs.body:
Doc tests are not a cargo target, so neither cargo-hack step in `rust-cargo-hack` compiles them: `check --each-feature` is lib-only and `check --tests` selects unit and integration test targets. The only job that compiles doc tests, `rust-doctest`, runs the whole workspace with all features, so feature unification lets a doc example compile against a dependency feature its crate never declares. The example on `OpProofsExEx` in `reth-optimism-exex` imports `OP_MAINNET`, which the chainspec crate exports only under `superchain-configs`, and has been broken for any crate-scoped run since #21397 while CI stayed green.

This adds a per-crate doc test pass with default features to `rust-doctest`, after the workspace-wide one. No effect on users; CI only.

**CI is expected to fail on this PR**: the new step catches the `reth-optimism-exex` doctest above. That fix goes in a separate PR so the gap and the instance stay distinct. Verified locally on develop: `cargo hack test --doc -p reth-optimism-exex` fails with `unresolved import reth_optimism_chainspec::OP_MAINNET`, while `just test-docs` passes.

The doctest step runs real builds, so it costs more than the existing `check`-only cargo-hack steps; it sits in `rust-doctest` (2xlarge.gen2, dev-profile build cache) rather than the memory-constrained `rust-cargo-hack` job for that reason.

Only packages with a lib or proc-macro target are selected, because `cargo test --doc` errors on a binary-only package (kona-node, lokahi, the examples) rather than skipping it.

Review notes from the CI config reviewer: the step runs real builds for 68 crates, unsharded, on the required path. This PR's run gives the first measurement of what that adds to `rust-doctest`; if it is large, the recipe already takes `partition`/`shuffle`/`seed` like its siblings so the step can be sharded the same way `rust-cargo-hack` is. Those parameters are unused by CI for now, kept for parity with `hack` and `hack-tests-default`.

First CI run (pipeline 136537): the step fails as intended, and on a second instance before it reaches the ExEx one. `kona-serde`'s README example calls `toml::from_str`, which `toml` only exports under its `serde` feature; the crate never enables it, so the example only compiles when another crate's `toml` features unify in. cargo-hack stops at the first failing package (40 of 68 run), so the ExEx doctest is not in this log yet.

Measured cost: `rust-doctest` took 22 minutes against about 6 minutes on develop. The workspace-wide pass took 4.5 minutes and the new step 16.7 minutes for 40 crates, so a full green pass is likely 25 to 30 minutes for this step alone. Sharding it with `--partition` across nodes, as `rust-cargo-hack` does, is the obvious follow-up if that is too much for the required path.

topPRs.title: op-node,op-alloy!: Remove unused interop block replacement deposit source
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
No code uses deposit source domain 4. An early interop design used it for block replacement deposits. The design changed, but the types stayed in op-node and op-alloy. This PR removes them and marks domain 4 as unused, like domain 3.

There is no effect on node operators or chains.

BREAKING CHANGE: op-alloy-consensus no longer exports `InteropBlockReplacementDepositSource`. The `InteropBlockReplacement` variants of `DepositSourceDomainIdentifier` and `DepositSourceDomain` are also removed. Downstream crates that use these items must delete those uses. The protocol does not use domain 4, so no replacement exists.

The Go, Rust and deletion review agents ran. They found only the missing breaking-change marker, which this PR now has.
